title: `palmux ptyhost` subcommand (pty mode) + socket protocol + cgroup-escape spawn

spike_first.goal: Confirm systemd-run --user --scope --collect places the child in a cgroup that survives `systemctl --user restart` of a sibling user unit.
steps: On this host (Ubuntu/home-manager class) run: `systemd-run --user --scope --collect --unit palmux-spike-$$ -- sleep 600` and capture the child PID.
Verify the child is in a DIFFERENT cgroup than the parent shell / a mock unit: `cat /proc/<pid>/cgroup` vs the launcher's cgroup.
Simulate the survival guarantee: start a throwaway `systemd --user` transient unit, restart it, confirm the systemd-run scope child is NOT killed.

Record whether D-Bus user session is present (`systemctl --user status`); if absent, exercise the setsid+double-fork fallback path and confirm detach (child reparented to pid 1, new session id via `ps -o sid`).
Note NixOS-appliance equivalence expectations (D-Bus user session present per ADR-0003) in decisions.json — full NixOS run deferred to SURVIVAL AC on real systemd.
spike_first.record_to: docs/sprint-logs/S3f2658/decisions.json (spike result: systemd-run available? cgroup isolated? fallback verified?)

acceptance_scenarios.intent: ptyhost spawns claude under a PTY with argv/env/cwd from palmux2 and serves the framed socket protocol with an absolute-offset ring.
steps: Unit: construct the framed protocol codec; round-trip encode/decode every message (HELLO, ATTACH, DATA, INPUT, RESIZE, ACK, STATUS, SHUTDOWN) and assert byte-exact framing + version field in HELLO.

Unit: Ring with absolute offsets — write N chunks, assert DATA replay from offset O returns bytes[O:] with correct absolute offset headers; assert offset=-1 replays from ring head; assert wrap/eviction advances the head offset (no offset reuse).

Integration: run `palmux ptyhost` (or the internal server directly) holding a fake claude (tests/testdata fake_claude or `cat`) under a real PTY; connect a unix-socket client, send HELLO, assert HELLO reply carries protocol version + mode=pty + pid + argv-hash.

Integration: ATTACH{offset:-1}, feed input via INPUT, assert echoed bytes arrive as DATA frames with monotonically increasing absolute offsets; send RESIZE{cols,rows} and assert the child sees the new winsize (fake child prints TIOCGWINSZ).
Integration: send STATUS request, assert response includes pid, alive=true, ring bytes, ring head offset.
acceptance_scenarios.expected: All frames round-trip; ring offsets are absolute and monotone; PTY spawn/resize/input/output all work over the socket.

acceptance_scenarios.intent: Spawn path tries systemd-run --user --scope --collect, falls back to setsid+double-fork on failure (runtime detection, ADR-0003).
steps: Unit: launcher with an injected exec runner — when systemd-run probe succeeds, assert the built argv is `systemd-run --user --scope --collect --unit palmux-agent-<instancePrefix>-<hash> -- <palmuxBin> ptyhost …`.
Unit: when the systemd-run probe returns non-zero / not-found, assert the launcher falls back to the setsid+double-fork detach path (no systemd-run in argv).
Unit: assert the scope --unit name embeds instancePrefix so INSTANCE=dev and host never collide.
Integration (host, real): actually launch a ptyhost via the launcher on this box; confirm it detaches (survives the launching process exit) — ties into AC-1-3 survival.
acceptance_scenarios.expected: Runtime detection picks systemd-run when available, setsid otherwise; scope name carries instancePrefix.

acceptance_scenarios.intent: [SURVIVAL] ptyhost + claude (same pid) survive `systemctl --user restart palmux2` and a `kill -9` of palmux2.
steps: Start a SEPARATE dev instance: `make serve INSTANCE=dev` (never touch host palmux2 — forbidden). This gives an independent palmux2 with its own instancePrefix (_pmx_dev_) and socket dir.

Wrap the dev instance in a transient user unit for the systemd path: `systemd-run --user --unit palmux2-survtest --scope -- <bin> serve --config-dir <tmp> --addr 127.0.0.1:<devport> --tmux-prefix _pmx_dev_` OR use an existing user-unit test harness; record the ptyhost child pid and claude pid.
Open a claude-tui tab (drive via API/WS on the dev port) so a ptyhost spawns; capture ptyhost pid and the claude pid from the STATUS response / status file.
SURVIVAL-A: `systemctl --user restart palmux2-survtest` (restart the palmux2 unit). After restart, assert the ptyhost pid AND the claude pid are STILL ALIVE (same pids) via `kill -0 <pid>` / `ps`.
SURVIVAL-B: `kill -9` the palmux2 process directly. Assert ptyhost + claude survive (same pids).
Assert the socket + status file still exist and STATUS still answers alive=true after each event. Log SURVIVAL_PASS x2.

If a real systemd --user session is genuinely unavailable in the runner, escalate at milestone (priority_rule 0) — do NOT silently mark done; the setsid fallback survival (kill -9 only) must still be demonstrated.
acceptance_scenarios.expected: ptyhost and claude keep the same pids across palmux2 restart and kill -9; STATUS remains alive. SURVIVAL_PASS.

acceptance_scenarios.intent: claude exit → ptyhost records exit status in STATUS response + status file, then exits itself (thin holder; respawn is palmux2's job).
steps: Hold a fake child that exits with a known code (e.g. `sh -c 'exit 7'`).
After the child exits, assert a STATUS request returns alive=false with exit status 7 (before the ptyhost tears down), and that the status JSON file on disk records the same exit status.
Assert the ptyhost process itself then exits (does NOT respawn — respawn is palmux2-side).
Assert no orphaned PTY fd / goroutine leak (clean shutdown).
acceptance_scenarios.expected: Exit status is recorded in both channels; ptyhost self-terminates without respawning.

notes: internal/ptyhost/ is a NEW package (ring w/ absolute offsets, framed protocol codec, socket server, launcher). cmd/palmux/ptyhost.go is the subcommand entry. ptyhost holds NO claude-specific knowledge — argv/env/cwd are opaque (ADR-0002). Protocol must be frozen-minimal (adding messages is an ADR-0002 violation signal).
